summary.text: Sue Shink is a Democratic state senator from Michigan State Senate District 14 who has served since January 1, 2023 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
A lawyer and farm owner, she previously chaired the Washtenaw County Board of Commissioners.

paragraphs.text: Sue Shink lives in Northfield Township, Michigan.

She earned a bachelor's degree in political science and government in 1989, a juris doctor in 1994 and a master's degree in resource policy and management in 1995, all from the University of Michigan.
Her career experience includes owning North Wind Farm LLC.
Shink chaired the Washtenaw County Board of Commissioners and served on the Washtenaw County Food Policy Council and the Huron River Watershed Council.

In a 2022 Ballotpedia survey, she described herself as "a mom, a lawyer and a public servant" and said her work on the county board included increased funding for safety-net services, a weatherization fund and efforts to address climate change.

In the Senate, Shink's 2025 and 2026 assignments include chairing the Natural Resources and Agriculture Committee and serving as majority vice chair of the Civil Rights, Judiciary, and Public Safety Committee.
She also sits on the Appropriations, Energy and Environment, Housing and Human Services, and Local Government committees.
